title: Songs Created By AI Banned From Australia's Music Charts
content:
Songs Created By AI Banned From Australia's Music Charts 19
			
		 	
				Australia's official music charts will no longer accept songs that are largely or entirely AI-generated, requiring eligible releases to be "substantially human made." The BBC reports:  The Australian Recording Industry Association (ARIA) said the new code would help "promote the human nature of artistry." It follows a controversy around a cover of Madonna's Like A Prayer by Australian DJ Josh Fawaz which recently topped the ARIA dance singles chart and peaked at number 2 on the country's overall chart. The song has become a staple of commercial radio station playlists and been streamed more than 48 million times on Spotify alone. Fawaz later added generative AI credits to the song after a backlash.
 
ARIA said that Australian artists were competing for attention "in the most crowded market in history" and that it was "not interested in promoting or celebrating the success of AI-generated music that does not contain human artistry." Under the new rules, AI assistance can still be used, but humans must have written the song, and have performed the lead vocal and primary instruments. AI can also still be used for mastering songs and, for example, using drum machines and auto tune. [...]
 
Artists will be required to declare AI use when they submit a song for chart consideration. ARIA said that if it later emerged music was largely AI-generated it could retrospectively adjust chart positions, and if the piece topped the charts, it may request that awards given for reaching Number One were returned. Artists and their representatives will be able to challenge their exclusion. ARIA chief executive Annabelle Herd said: "These changes reflect our intent to remain dynamic and promote the human nature of artistry in what is, to say the least, a rapidly developing space. Artists already use AI tools in their work, the charts can and should evolve to keep room for that, but music generated wholesale by services built on artists' recordings is a different matter."
 
She added: "A chart that rewards unlicensed AI output would undercut the very basis of the recorded music we exist to represent."

report.summary: 澳大利亚官方排行榜禁止主要AI生成的歌曲上榜，要求必须为人类实质创作。
report.background: 随着AI音乐生成工具普及，大量全自动或半自动生成的音乐涌入流媒体和排行榜，引发对艺术性和版权的争议。导火索是澳大利亚DJ Josh Fawaz的AI翻唱版《Like A Prayer》登顶ARIA舞曲榜，并在总榜达到第2名，播放量巨大，随后在舆论压力下补充了AI credits。ARIA因此推出新规，强调上榜作品须“实质性人类制作”，以促进人类艺术性，同时保留AI辅助工具的空间。此举反映音乐产业在AI时代重新界定创作主体与价值认可的行业趋势。
key_points: 新规要求上榜歌曲必须由人类创作词曲、演唱主唱并演奏主要乐器，AI生成部分不能为主体。
导火索是DJ Fawaz的AI翻唱歌曲登顶排行榜，大量流媒体播放后引发争议，促使ARIA紧急修订规则。
AI辅助仍被允许，包括母带处理、鼓机、自动调音等，规则旨在区分“工具”与“全自动生成”。
艺术家需主动申报AI使用情况，若违反规定，榜单可追溯调整名次，甚至要求退回榜首奖项。
report.impact: 对AI行业而言，这为AI音乐公司划出更清晰的分界线，可能促使他们转向辅助创作而非全自动生成。对开发者而言，需要开发合规的AI工具或AI生成内容检测服务，以帮助平台方把关。对普通用户而言，排行榜将更强调人类创作的价值，但AI音乐仍可在其他平台和场景存在，用户的收听选择权依然广泛。整体上，该政策将倒逼AI音乐生态更透明、更尊重版权。
report.tools: 关注AI音乐生成器Suno、Udio，以及开源模型Meta MusicGen、Stable Audio，可快速体验AI创作能力。若想推动“人类创作+AI辅助”，可使用LANDR做母带，用ACR服务（如音频指纹识别）检测AI痕迹，确保作品符合排行榜要求。
